title: Flat White with Velvety Microfoam
summary: A double espresso in a 160 ml cup with silky, barely aerated steamed milk and a thin microfoam heart on top.
equipment: milk jug (350 ml) with a pointed spout

ingredients.note: about 120 ml ends up in the cup

steps.title: Pull the shot
steps.text: Pull a double espresso, 18 g in and about 40 ml out, into the warm cup. The smaller cup keeps the coffee flavour strong.

steps.title: Texture the milk
steps.text: Let in air for just 2-3 s, then spin the milk to 60-65 °C. The foam should be thin and silky, about 5 mm deep, with no visible bubbles.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Pour from high in a thin stream so the milk blends under the crema, until the cup is about two-thirds full.

steps.title: Pour the heart
steps.text: Bring the spout close to the surface and let a round white disc spread, then lift slightly and draw the stream through the middle to make a heart.

tips: The key mistake is too much foam; a flat white should look flat and glossy, not domed.
Grind a touch finer than usual for a more concentrated shot.
Swirl the jug just before pouring to keep the microfoam blended.
storage: Serve immediately. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
